messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming route /v1/stream p95 breached SLO in region-us-west — p95=680ms (SLO 500ms), p99=2.3s. Multiple streaming stalls observed, client-side timeouts increasing. paging: oncall-maya. :rotating_light:
oncall-maya: acknowledged. I’m on it. grabbing metrics and starting triage — will update in 5.
runtime-liam: @oncall-maya any clue if this is model-side or infra?
oncall-maya: initial trace shows tail spikes on the serving nodes in pool-gpu-shared-4. signature: long queue wait + high write_io wait on node gpu-node-12.
sre-deepa: pulling node telemetry now — iowait jumped ~8x at 16:03 UTC, nvme saturated, also see sustained kernel_sched delays.
ops-jen: @liam can you check if there were recent rollouts that might correlate? deploy-bot: deploy v2.13.1 to runtime pool-gpu-shared-4 completed 15:58 UTC (sha: ab12f3).
runtime-liam: no heavy model change in that deploy. suspect noisy tenant causing shared NVMe/GPU bus pressure.
oncall-maya: running quick commands, pasting snippets:
```
# top-ish snapshot from gpu-node-12
15:59:02 up 3:23,  2 users,  load average: 6.12, 5.98, 3.21
%Cpu(s): 85.3 us,  5.2 sy,  0.0 ni,  9.5 id
iowait: 35.2%
nvidia-smi: processes: PID 2345 (tenant-a) GPU0 98% util, PID 9876 (tenant-b) 92% util
```

sre-deepa: iostat output shows >400MB/s writes and high await on nvme0n1. blkio throttle counters incrementing per cgroup for tenant-a.
ops-jen: so multi-tenant disk/PCIe saturation + GPU high occupancy — classic noisy-neighbor. we should mitigate live: options = throttle tenant, evict tenant pods from node, or route traffic to fallback model on less-burdened pool.
runtime-liam: can we do a quick eviction for the top offending tenant to reduce tail? suggest cordon node & evict tenant-a pods first. command:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep tenant-a | xargs -n1 kubectl delete pod -n runtime
```

oncall-maya: executing cordon + eviction now. will monitor p95.
(2m later)
oncall-maya: cordon done, evicted 6 pods for tenant-a. traffic started draining.
incident-bot: Event: pods evicted from gpu-node-12 by oncall-maya at 16:07 UTC.
sre-deepa: immediate improvement in p95 — dropped from 680ms -> 420ms within 40s. p99 still high ~1.1s but trending down. streaming stalls reduced.
support-nora: are there affected customers to notify? pulling recent 5xx/timeout logs for the route.
cs-amy: shortlist: customer IDs 1245, 6672, 9921 saw transient errors between 15:58-16:10 UTC. impacted by retries/timeouts, some short-lived streaming disconnects. preparing customer note.
runtime-liam: also enabled temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated pool-d1 for /v1/stream for high priority tenants until we fully stabilize. config snippet:
```
route /v1/stream {
  prefer_pool: pool-d1
  fallback: pool-gpu-shared-4
}
```

ops-jen: added a QoS throttle on tenant-a cgroup to cap write bandwidth to 100MB/s as an intermediate control. applied at 16:11 UTC.
sre-deepa: after throttle and eviction + routing change: p95=390ms, p99=820ms, streaming stall rate down ~90%.
oncall-maya: handing off to runtime-liam and sre-deepa for follow-up and RCA. I’ll keep an eye for 15m.
runtime-liam: assigning issue-INC-2026-581 to runtime for root cause. immediate next steps: collect full nvme SMART logs, kernel slab/stack traces from gpu-node-12, pod-level IO histograms, and tenant-a workload traces.
sre-deepa: will also validate cgroup blkio thresholds and whether our autoscaler moved IO-heavy tenants onto shared nodes.
support-nora: sent interim customer message to the 3 impacted accounts with a brief explanation and ETA for post-incident report.
cs-amy: customers asked for timeline — ETA 3 hours for preliminary RCA.
oncall-maya: final operational note: mitigation ladder used = cordon+evict -> apply cgroup throttle -> route to dedicated pool. impact window ~ 15:58-16:12 UTC, majority mitigated by 16:10.
runtime-liam: plan for post-incident: 1) tighten placement policy to avoid colocating high-nvme tenants on shared pools, 2) add autoscaler filter for IO-metrics, 3) promote dedicated routing for known latency-sensitive customers.
sre-deepa: logging follow-ups and metrics snapshots attached to INC-2026-581. tagging ops/placement team for policy change.
oncall-maya: thanks team. I’m closing the on-call page but leaving thread open for RCA notes. :white_check_mark:
support-nora: tagging legal/compliance for any required notes — none expected.
deploy-bot: scheduled a targeted maintenance window for pool-gpu-shared-4 nodes at 02:00 UTC to drain and run disk health checks.
ops-jen: follow-up action items: add per-tenant IO budgets, alert when node nvme bandwidth >70% for 1m, and create a playbook for live eviction + routing rule steps.
runtime-liam: noted. will draft playbook and share here.
(THREAD END)
